profile.title: Profile
profile.description: Your name appears in the workspace’s activity.
profile.name: Name

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: Saved in your copy and applied on all your devices.

language.title: Language
language.description: The app speaks it on all your devices, and new boards get their default columns in it.

accessKey.title: Access key
accessKey.description: It’s what you use to sign in to this copy. Generating a new one signs out your other sessions. It doesn’t affect the vault’s master password.
accessKey.newDescription: The old key no longer works, and your other sessions have been signed out. It’s shown only once.

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.description: Agent tokens and projects belong to a specific workspace.
workspace.name: Workspace name
workspace.deleteDescription: Its projects, boards, documents, attachments, trash and tokens will be deleted. This can’t be undone.

copy.title: This copy
copy.description: The version of Orqevio you’re running. Your copy checks for new versions at most every 12 hours.

how.button: Merge the Dependabot pull request in your copy’s repository, and it deploys itself. If you don’t see one, bump the create-orqevio version in its package.json.
how.source: In the repository, then restart the server:

version.kept: Your data, access key and vault are preserved.

backups.title: Backups
backups.description: Every day this copy backs itself up: everything as it is, the encrypted vault, the trash, the history and the attachments included. The last 7 are kept, apart from its data.
backups.whereFolder: They’re in the server’s folder {{name}}. To keep them on another disk or volume, set BACKUP_DIR.
backups.whereBucket: They’re in the R2 bucket {{name}} of your Cloudflare account, apart from the attachments.
backups.none: No backups yet: the first one is made within the hour.
backups.missingFiles_one: {{count}} attachment couldn’t be copied into it.
backups.missingFiles_other: {{count}} attachments couldn’t be copied into it.
backups.newer: Made with Orqevio {{version}}: update this copy to restore it.
backups.keep_one: The last daily backup is kept, and the one made before the last restore.
backups.keep_other: The last {{count}} daily backups are kept, and the one made before the last restore.
backups.restoreDescription: This copy goes back to how it was on {{date}}.
backups.restoreLoses: Everything goes back: workspaces, documents, cards, vault, agents, trash and history. What changed since is lost.
backups.restoreSafety: First, a backup of the copy as it is now is made and kept apart, so you can come back to it.
backups.restoreSessions: Every session ends. You stay signed in here, and your access key is the one you use now.
backups.restoreAgents: Agents whose access you have taken away since then don’t get it back.

problem.title: Backups can’t be made there
problem.access: Orqevio (the server’s user {{user}}) can’t read or write {{path}}. Give the backups folder back to it: mounted from the server, with sudo chown -R {{user}} on it; inside the volume (what docker compose cp copies in is left to root), with docker compose run --rm --user root app chown -R orqevio:orqevio {{root}}.

damaged.title_one: {{count}} attachment of this backup is damaged or gone:
damaged.title_other: {{count}} attachments of this backup are damaged or gone:
damaged.body: This copy stays as it is. If you restore without them, their cards and documents come back, but these files don’t.

export.title: Export your data
export.description: A ZIP to read your data or take it elsewhere: the tasks of each workspace in JSON, its documents in Markdown and the attachments. Without the vault, which has its own encrypted export, nor the history or the trash.

erase.title: Erase this copy
erase.description: Permanently erases your workspaces, your vault and your tokens. The copy will ask for the setup code again.
erase.confirmDescription: This can’t be undone. Enter your access key to confirm.

uninstall.title: Uninstall Orqevio
uninstall.description: Deletes everything for good, attachments included, and leaves this copy unusable. Then it shows how to remove the copy itself from your Cloudflare account or your server.
uninstall.confirmDescription: This can’t be undone. You’ll lose:

loses.data: Your workspaces, projects, boards and documents.
loses.vault: Your vault. To keep it, export an encrypted copy from the vault first.
loses.agents: Your agents’ access and every session.

uninstall.afterwards: This is step 1 of 2. In step 2 you’ll see how to remove the copy itself from your Cloudflare account or your server.
uninstall.oneCommand: Installed it with the command? From your computer, {{command}} does both steps at once.

keep.label: Keep them
keep.hint: A copy installed again with the same name, or with the same backups folder, can restore them. Delete them by hand when you no longer need them.

delete.label: Delete them too
delete.hint: Nothing of this copy can be brought back afterwards.
